sentences.text:
The case of the claimants is that on 15.12.2016 at about 07.00 P.M. When one Ramesh Kumar,
who is the petitioner in MCOP.No.460 of 2017 was riding TVS XL moped, bearing Reg. No.TN 41 D 4965 along with Ramesh, who is the petitioner in MCOP.No.461 of 2017 as pillion rider, at that time,
a car bearing Reg. No. TN 41 AC 7725 which was driven by its driver and the same is owned by the second respondent and insured with the appellant herein, in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. TN 41 S 9716 driven by one Kanniyappan, dashed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 30/04/2025 04:31:56 pm ) against the claimants moped, due to which, the rider of the moped and the pillion rider fell down on the road and sustained injuries and admitted in the hospital.
Thereafter, the two injured filed a separate claim petitions before the Tribunal claiming compensation.
3. Before the Tribunal, the claimants examined three witnesses as P.W.1 to 3 and marked Exs.P-1 to P-29.
On the side of the insurance company, no witness was examined and no documentary evidence was marked.

The Tribunal, considering the evidence, both oral and documentary, awarded compensation, in favour of the claimants, in a sum of Rs.6,81,500/- and Rs.16,28,000/-
respectively.

Aggrieved by the said compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the insurance company filed appeal questioning the quantum of compensation and one of the claimant has filed cross objection seeking enhancement.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that in respect of MCOP. No.460 of 2017 is concerned, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is excessive.
The Tribunal erred in fixing compensation towards disability and loss of earning power in absence https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 30/04/2025 04:31:56 pm ) of any sufficient evidence and also the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings is also highly excessive.
Without following the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the Tribunal has awarded huge compensation, which is un-sustainable and the same is liable to be quashed.
Hence, the learned counsel prays that this Court may interfere with the award and allow this petition.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that in respect of MCOP. No.461 of 2017 is concerned, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal for a sum of Rs.6,81,500/- is highly excessive.

The Tribunal erred in fixing compensation towards disability and loss of earning power in absence of any sufficient evidence and also the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings is also very high.
Without following the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the Tribunal has awarded huge compensation, which is unsustainable and the same is liable to be quashed.
Hence, the learned counsel prays that this Court may interfere with the award and allow this petition.

sentences.text: claimant sustained injuries all over the body and fracture in shaft of tibia and fibula left lef, loss of skin in left leg posterior and medial aspect, extensor tendon laceration left ankle, multiple abrasion wound over scalp, face and left shoulder.
Under such circumstances, the claimant is not able to discharge his daily life and the claimant were performed five surgeries.
Hence, the Tribunal ought have taken 100% disability to award reasonable compensation on the head of functional disability.

Further, the Court below ought to have appreciate that for the aforesaid injuries sustained by the cross objector five surgeries were performed and in future, doctor instructed that two surgeries have to be performed, hence, the Court below ought to have consider the reasonable award on considering the nature of injuries sustained by the cross objector.

7. The learned counsel further submitted that the cross objector was taking treatment in the hospital at intensive care unit for more than 10 days and as inpatient for more than two months and thereafter, taking continuous treatment as outpatient till today, hence the court below ought to have award https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 30/04/2025 04:31:56 pm ) reasonable compensation on the head of attendar charges, Extra nourishment, future medical expenses and transportation charges.

At the time of accident, the cross objector was having auto and earned monthly income of Rs.20,000/- and after the accident, the cross objector is not able to continue his duty, hence the court below ought not to have fix Rs.7,500/- along as monthly income of the cross objector to award compensation on the head of disability.
Further, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.3,000/- towards extra nourishment and not awarded any compensation towards attendar charges.
This Court may interfere with the impugned award and allow the cross objection.

8. The learned counsel for the claimant in MCOP. No.460 of 2017 submitted that the Tribunal after considering the witness and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.6,81,500/- which is perfectly in order, which needs no interference.

9. This Court gave its anxious consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel appearing on either side and also perused the oral and documentary evidence and the judgment passed by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 30/04/2025 04:31:56 pm )
Tribunal.
10. The factum of the case are not in dispute.
The manner of the accident is also not in dispute.

The only issue that arises for consideration is with regard to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads, according to the appellant/insurance company, which is highly excessive.
In the instant case, the injured was aged about 28 years at the time of the accident and he was doing mason work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month
. The Tribunal has fixed the notional monthly income at Rs.7,500/- including future prospects since there was no proof regarding the avocation or the monthly income of the injured claimant.
The accident had taken place on 15.12.2016.
Without perusing the proof, the notional monthly income fixed by the Tribunal is higher side.
Considering the age of the claimant and also the year in which the accident had taken place, this Court is inclined to modify the notional monthly income at Rs.5,000/-.
